Flooding Hits Fisheries Industry Sites in Saudi Arabia, Disrupting Operations

A powerful storm system has triggered widespread flooding across several key aquaculture zones in Saudi Arabia, severely impacting the Fisheries industry’s production sites and workforce. The event, which began on Monday and continues to unfold, has inundated low-lying fish farms and hatcheries along the Red Sea coast and in the Eastern Province, causing significant operational disruptions.

Initial assessments from the Saudi Fisheries Association estimate that more than 30% of coastal aquaculture facilities in the Jazan and Al Khobar regions have sustained flood damage. “Water levels rose rapidly, overwhelming our containment ponds and damaging essential equipment,” said Saeed Al-Harbi, spokesperson for the association. “Many facilities are struggling to maintain adequate conditions for their stocks, and there is a real risk of loss if the flooding persists.”

At Al Noor Aquatic, a major operator in the region, management reported that several of its breeding tanks were breached, with thousands of fish escaping into floodwaters. “Our teams are working around the clock to salvage what they can, but the situation remains very challenging,” said company operations manager Fadwa Al-Qahtani. “We are prioritizing staff safety and the welfare of our remaining stocks.”

Industry workers have also been affected, with some unable to access their workplaces due to submerged access roads operated by the farms. “We are facing the double challenge of property damage and the inability of our staff to reach the sites,” said Mohammed Al-Mutairi, HR director at Red Sea Fisheries Group. Many employees have been temporarily relocated to safe areas within company accommodation complexes, while emergency teams remain on-site to monitor infrastructure and support ongoing rescue efforts.

The Saudi Union of Fisheries Workers has called for immediate support for affected workers. “Our members’ livelihoods are at stake,” said union chairperson Reem Al-Dossary. “We urge all companies to ensure their safety and to provide necessary assistance until operations can safely resume.”

As the storm continues, industry analysts warn that prolonged flooding could further disrupt production and rehabilitation efforts. The Saudi Fisheries Association is currently coordinating with member companies to assess damages and develop a recovery strategy once conditions improve.
